A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, renamed from StereoGen to ZeroStereo. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison across renaming, renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original stereo-model evaluations, module and loss ablations, synthesis comparisons, and DrivingStereo weather results, including supplementary Tables 5–7.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds disparity statistics, synthesis resource measurements, edge-error evaluation and reconstruction measurements in Tables 2, 4, 6 and 9.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 6 retain the same depth estimation, diffusion inpainting, flip-based confidence, adaptive disparity sampling, disparity dilation and masked training losses. Equations 1–8 are unchanged apart from naming; the StereoGen-to-ZeroStereo renaming does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: The added DKT-RAFT comparison uses a model fine-tuned on Booster, explicitly stated in v2 Table 7. Otherwise, the proposed pipeline's training collections and evaluation coverage remain unchanged. Middlebury 2014/2021 visualizations and DrivingStereo weather tests were already present in v1.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds DKT-RAFT and Former-RAFT while removing ITSA-PSMNet and ITSA-GwcNet from v1 Table 4; ITSA-CFNet remains. Synthesis comparisons also expand through actual RePaint resource measurements and AdaMPI qualitative evaluation. StereoDiffusion, already evaluated in v1, receives additional comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds distinct auxiliary protocols: edge-restricted stereo scoring, reconstruction evaluation using AbsErr/SSIM/Lp, resolution-specific resource measurements, and an AdaMPI camera-motion-ratio sweep at 0.1, 0.3 and 0.5. Core stereo splits and training budgets remain unchanged. RePaint's 256×256 resource setting differs from the other methods' 512×512 setting.

E4.justification: Beyond retained module, loss and weather analyses, v2 examines ADS disparity distributions, edge accuracy, synthesis resource costs and reconstruction consistency (Tables 2, 4, 6 and 9). New StereoDiffusion failure examples and AdaMPI motion sensitivity substantially expand diagnostics. Some existing qualitative examples are replaced or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. The new mean/maximum disparity summaries characterize generated data rather than experimental uncertainty; the method's confidence-map computation is unchanged.

E6.justification: Most shared benchmark values remain unchanged, but substantial auxiliary results and comparator entries are added. In Table 1, ADS+Inpainting+TCG changes Midd-T (H) Noc EPE from 2.34 to 2.18 and >2px error from 7.33% to 7.11%. New Table 9 reports reconstruction SSIM of 0.269 for StereoDiffusion versus 0.850 for the proposed method. v2 also reports training convergence difficulties with StereoDiffusion pairs. Its 31.2-second timing at 512×512 replaces v1's approximately 40-second statement without establishing a same-setting speedup.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, flip-invariance reasoning, sampling formulation and losses in Equations 1–8 are retained. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs, and v2 introduces no new mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same core contributions: single-image stereo synthesis using fine-tuned diffusion, TCG and ADS, enabling state-of-the-art zero-shot matching with approximately Scene Flow-sized training data. The revised title makes an existing objective more explicit.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations about MPI artifacts undermining stereo training and superior edge accuracy. It removes v1's explanation of TCG's Middlebury learning trade-off and claims consistent improvement despite remaining mixed ablation results. The edge-superiority wording also overlooks Table 6's lower Midd-T EPE for NS65K, 2.24 versus 2.35. The concluding limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code availability; v2 supplies a repository address, whose actual availability is not established by the PDFs. v2 identifies RAFT-Stereo as the backbone for the retained loss ablation. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit 22 training/32 evaluation update counts and inherited iterative-loss-weight statement. Most implementation details remain.

R1.justification: The research-positioning framework remains, with added references covering AdaMPI/MPI, DKT-RAFT, Former-RAFT, monocular-depth background and other supporting work. Alternative synthesis methods receive expanded discussion. Section 4.5 drops v1's priority claim of being first below 10% Midd-T full-resolution non-occluded error.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, experimental discussion and supplementary prose while renaming the paper and method. The appendix places synthesis-method discussion before additional NeRF-Stereo comparisons. This is substantial editorial and narrative revision despite stable core scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 adds four tables and new Figures 9–10, redraws Figure 2's training branch, and restructures the benchmark table. The StereoDiffusion comparison enters the main text with replacement examples; KITTI visualizations move to the appendix and gain an example. Figure 5 loses one example, while existing Middlebury, ETH3D and DrivingStereo displays are largely retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens assessment of the unchanged method through updated stereo comparisons and quantitative synthesis-quality, efficiency and edge analyses. Code access information and loss-ablation provenance also improve documentation. These benefits are tempered by underspecified new evaluation procedures, omitted iteration counts, and edge/TCG interpretations that overstate their tables, supporting a limited net improvement.
